mainTopic: Disrespect for חכמים as אפיקורסות, and the future reward of צדיקים (סנהדרין 100a)
overview: The גמרא continues defining an אפיקורס, someone who shows disrespect for the חכמים. רבא answers the mocker who said the rabbis never 'permit a raven or forbid a dove'. רב פפא, רב יהודה and רב נחמן add more examples: saying 'those rabbis', speaking lightly of the מגילת אסתר, or calling your teacher by name, as גיחזי did. A story about רבי יוחנן's teaching on giant jewel gates for ירושלים shows that a student who believes the חכמים only after seeing for himself is really mocking them. The גמרא then explains the 'healing leaves' of the river from the בית המקדש, and teaches that those who toil and go hungry for תורה will shine and be satisfied in עולם הבא. Finally it discusses how vast the reward of צדיקים is, and רבי מאיר's rule of 'measure for measure'. רבי מאיר's answer to רבי יהושע continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The complaint that the rabbis add nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the mocking claim that the חכמים never permit anything the תורה forbids and never forbid anything the תורה permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The rabbis have never] permitted a raven for us, nor have they forbidden a dove for us.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the words of the person being described as an אפיקורס. He is mocking the חכמים and saying they are useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The raven is clearly not kosher, and the dove is clearly kosher. The mocker means that the rabbis only repeat what the תורה already says outright, so in his view they add nothing. This is the attitude that makes someone an אפיקורס.

keyTerms.meaning: A raven, a bird the תורה lists as not kosher

phrases.english: they have not permitted a raven for us,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that began just before, 'The rabbis have never...'. The speaker is mocking them.

phrases.english: and they have not forbidden a dove for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁרוֹ לַן עוֹרְבָא, וְלָא אֲסַרוּ לַן יוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the description of the mocker, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying that the rabbis are useless because they only repeat the obvious is the talk of an אפיקורס.

steps.title: רבא shows the rabbis really do permit 'ravens' and forbid 'doves'
steps.stepSummary: When animals from the family of בנימין were brought to רבא, he pointed out each time that his ruling went beyond what was obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they would bring a possible טריפה from the house of בנימין before רבא: if he found a reason to permit it, he would say, 'See, I am permitting a raven for you.' If he found a reason to forbid it, he would say, 'See, I am forbidding a dove for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבא that answers the mocker's complaint through actual rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that looks like a טריפה seems forbidden, just as a raven is forbidden. When רבא permitted it, he was 'permitting a raven.' An animal that looks fine seems permitted, just as a dove is permitted. When he forbade it, he was 'forbidding a dove.' This shows that the חכמים' rulings decide things the plain תורה text does not.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that may be a טריפה (fatally damaged, so not kosher)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rabbis' rulings decide real questions that the plain תורה text does not answer.

phrases.english: Rava: when they would bring
a possible tereifa of the house of Binyamin before him,
phrases.notes: Binyamin's family are the people the mocking complaint is tied to, so רבא answers them directly.

phrases.english: when he would see in it
a reason to permit it, he would say to them:
See that I am permitting a raven for you.
When he would see in it
a reason to forbid it, he would say to them:
See that I am forbidding a dove for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא, כִּי הֲווֹ מַיְיתִי טְרֵיפְתָּא דְּבֵי בִנְיָמִין קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mocker's claim from Step 1 through רבא's actual practice.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the rabbis never add anything beyond the plain תורה text.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rabbis' rulings on טריפות really do permit what looks forbidden and forbid what looks permitted.

steps.title: רב פפא: saying 'those rabbis' is a sign of an אפיקורס
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives another example of an אפיקורס: someone who refers to scholars as 'those rabbis.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: [An אפיקורס is] like someone who says 'those rabbis.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds his own definition of an אפיקורס. Even a small dismissive phrase counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes further than open mockery. Just pointing at scholars as 'those rabbis,' with a tone of looking down on them, already shows disrespect for the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Those rabbis,' said in a dismissive way

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Like one who says: 'Those rabbis.'
phrases.notes: He is still answering the earlier question, 'Who is an אפיקורס?'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּאָמַר הָנֵי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new, milder example of an אפיקורס alongside the mocker's words in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking of scholars dismissively as 'those rabbis' counts as אפיקורסות.

steps.title: רב פפא slips and fasts
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא once said 'like those rabbis' by mistake, and he fasted to make up for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא forgot himself and said, 'like those rabbis,' and he sat in a fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing how seriously רב פפא took his own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an accidental slip of the tongue felt to him like disrespect for the חכמים, so he fasted to gain atonement. This shows his rule from Step 3 was meant seriously, not just as advice for others.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa forgot and said:
'Like those rabbis,'
and he sat in a fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב פפא applying his own rule from Step 3 to himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even an accidental dismissive phrase about scholars calls for atonement.

steps.title: Mending the covers of holy scrolls
steps.stepSummary: Two scholars mending the covers for the scrolls of רב יהודה's school said that the מגילת אסתר does not need a cover.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי בר שמואל and רב הונא בר חייא were mending the covers of the scrolls of רב יהודה's school. When they reached the מגילת אסתר, they said: 'This [מגילת אסתר] does not need a cover.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. This step sets up the situation and the remark that will be criticized in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They felt the מגילת אסתר is less important than the other holy scrolls, so it does not need a protective cloth. Their remark is the setup for the response that follows.

phrases.aramaic: לֵוִי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל וְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Levi bar Shmuel and Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya
were mending
the covers of the scrolls of the school of Rav Yehuda.
When they reached the scroll of Esther, they said:
This [scroll of Esther] does not need a cover.
phrases.notes: Some versions just say 'this one'; others add the words in square brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵוִי בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל וְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא הֲווֹ קָא מְתַקְּנִי מִטְפְּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story, still on the theme of disrespect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scholars claimed the מגילת אסתר does not need a cover.

steps.title: Even that kind of talk looks like disrespect
steps.stepSummary: They are told that speaking this way about a holy scroll also looks like אפקירותא, the disrespect of an אפיקורס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Talk like this also looks like disrespect.
steps.whatsHappening: Their remark is rejected. Speaking lightly of the מגילת אסתר is called a kind of disrespect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נמי ('also') links this to the earlier examples. Just as dismissive words about scholars are disrespect, dismissive words about a holy scroll are too. So the idea of אפיקורסות is extended from people to holy objects.

keyTerms.meaning: Disrespect, the attitude of an אפיקורס

steps.whatToRemember: An אפיקורס is not only someone who openly mocks. Even small dismissive words, like 'those rabbis' or 'this scroll,' said about חכמים or holy things, count as disrespect.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: This seems to be רב יהודה, whose school's scrolls they were mending.

phrases.english: Something like this, too,
looks like disrespect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא נָמֵי מִיחְזֵי כִּי אַפְקֵירוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the scholars' remark from Step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The scholars' dismissive words about the מגילת אסתר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Speaking lightly of a holy scroll looks like the disrespect of an אפיקורס.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Calling your teacher by his name
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives another definition of an אפיקורס: someone who calls his רבי by his plain name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: an אפיקורס is a person who calls his teacher by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another opinion about who counts as an אפיקורס. רב נחמן says it is someone who calls his teacher by his plain name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier opinions spoke about disrespecting scholars in general. רב נחמן focuses on a student's relationship with his own רבי. Using the teacher's name with no title, as if he were an ordinary person, is the kind of disrespect that makes someone an אפיקורס.

keyTerms.meaning: One who calls his teacher by his name

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
This is one who calls his teacher by his name,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: זֶה הַקּוֹרֵא רַבּוֹ בִּשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another definition of an אפיקורס alongside רב פפא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calling one's teacher by his plain name is a mark of an אפיקורס.

steps.title: Proof from Gehazi, who called Elisha by name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says גיחזי was punished for calling his teacher אלישע by name, as shown in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: Why was גיחזי punished? Because he called his teacher by name, as the פסוק says: 'And גיחזי said: My lord the king, this is the woman and this is her son, whom אלישע revived.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב נחמן with a teaching of רבי יוחנן. גיחזי was punished because he called his teacher אלישע by his plain name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, גיחזי speaks to the king and says 'whom אלישע revived' instead of 'my master.' רבי יוחנן reads this as a real sin worthy of punishment. That shows calling your רבי by name is serious, which backs up רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: The servant and student of the prophet אֱלִישָׁע

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
For what reason was Gehazi punished?
Because he called his teacher by his name,
as it is said:
"And Gehazi said: My lord the king,
this is the woman and this is her son,
whom Elisha revived."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 8:5. Look at the last word: he says just 'אלישע' and not 'my master.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶעֱנַשׁ גֵּיחֲזִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source supporting רב נחמן's definition.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's claim that calling one's teacher by name is grave disrespect.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching that גיחזי was punished for saying 'אלישע' in מלכים ב 8:5.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה teaches about the river from the קדשי הקדשים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה, sitting before רבי זירא, teaches that in the future a river will flow from the קדשי הקדשים with fruit trees on its banks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה sat before רבי זירא and said: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring out a river from the קדשי הקדשים, and along it will grow all kinds of delicious fruit, as the פסוק in יחזקאל describes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. This teaching sets up the next move: someone will react to it, and that reaction raises a question about disrespect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content of the teaching is about the future, based on a פסוק in יחזקאל. What matters for our topic is what happens after he teaches it. This step is the background for the question about אפקירותא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy of Holies, the innermost room of the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya sat before Rabbi Zeira,
and he sat and said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined
to bring out a river from the Holy of Holies,
and along it all kinds of delicacies,
as it is said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְעַל הַנַּחַל יַעֲלֶה עַל שְׂפָתוֹ מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה
phrases.english: "And by the river, upon its bank, on this side and on that side, shall grow

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֵץ מַאֲכָל לֹא יִבּוֹל עָלֵהוּ
phrases.english: every tree for food, whose leaf shall not wither,
and its fruit shall not run out; every month it shall bring new fruit,
because its waters come out from the Sanctuary,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, so the line matches the פסוק.

phrases.english: and its fruit shall be for food and its leaf for healing."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 47:12.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that will test what counts as אפקירותא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future a river with wondrous fruit trees will flow from the קדשי הקדשים.

steps.title: Is saying 'well said' to a scholar disrespectful?
steps.stepSummary: An old man tells רבי ירמיה 'well said,' adding that רבי יוחנן said 'well said' too. רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether this kind of comment looks like disrespect.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain old man said to him: 'Well said,' and so said רבי יוחנן: 'Well said.' רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: Does something like this look like אפקירותא?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone praises רבי ירמיה's teaching, and רבי ירמיה wonders if that praise is actually disrespectful. He asks רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned (step 6) that some careless remarks count as אפקירותא. רבי ירמיה worries that an ordinary person 'approving' a scholar's teaching is like grading him, which might also be disrespect. He wants to know where the line is.

keyTerms.meaning: Well said, literally 'may it be straight'
Disrespect, the behavior of an אפיקורס

phrases.english: A certain old man said to him: "Well said,"
and so said Rabbi Yochanan: "Well said."

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
Does something like this look like disrespect?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the story to ask whether approving a scholar's words counts as אפקירותא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a non-scholar telling a חכם 'well said' is disrespect.

steps.title: רבי זירא: He is supporting you
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the old man was supporting רבי ירמיה, which is not disrespect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But he is supporting you!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question. Agreeing with and backing up a scholar is support, not disrespect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man was agreeing with רבי ירמיה's teaching and even added that רבי יוחנן said the same thing. That is honor for the teaching, not an insult. So simple agreement is not אפקירותא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
But he is supporting you!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the round-bracket words; with the square-bracket words it reads 'this one is supporting you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Agreeing with a scholar is support, not disrespect.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's teaching about giant gemstone gates
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains which kind of 'support' really is disrespect, and begins with רבי יוחנן's teaching about huge jewels for the gates of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if you heard about such a thing, this is what you heard: like when רבי יוחנן sat and taught that הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring jewels thirty by thirty אמות, carve an opening ten wide and twenty high, and set them as the gates of ירושלים, as the פסוק says.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא says there IS a kind of 'agreeing' that is disrespect, and he starts telling a story to show it. This teaching is setup for the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא grants that רבי ירמיה may have heard that some 'support' is disrespectful. He points to a specific case to show what it looks like. First he gives רבי יוחנן's teaching, which will be mocked and then 'confirmed' in the wrong way.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא, שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ:
phrases.english: Rather, if you heard about this, this is what you heard:
phrases.notes: He means: if you heard that 'supporting' a scholar can be disrespect, it was about a case like this one.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְקָא דָרֵישׁ:
phrases.english: like that case where Rabbi Yochanan sat and taught:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to bring
precious stones and pearls
that are thirty by thirty cubits,
and He carves in them an opening ten wide by twenty high,
and He sets them up as the gates of Jerusalem,
as it is said:
"And I will make your windows of rubies,
and your gates of carbuncle stones, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 54:12.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא, שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After saying simple agreement is fine, רבי זירא begins the case where 'agreement' is disrespect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, giant jewels will serve as the gates of ירושלים.

steps.title: A student mocks רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A student makes fun of רבי יוחנן: today we cannot even find a jewel the size of a small bird's egg, so how will we find such huge ones?
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain student mocked him and said: Now we cannot even find a jewel the size of a little dove's egg, and we will find one this big?
steps.whatsHappening: A student challenges רבי יוחנן's teaching, but in a mocking way. He says it is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student judges רבי יוחנן's words only by what he sees today. He is not asking to learn; he is scoffing. This attitude is the root of the disrespect the story is about.

keyTerms.meaning: The egg of a small dove-like bird

phrases.english: A certain student mocked him,
he said:
Now we do not even find a jewel the size of a small dove's egg,
and we will find one this big?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The student attacks רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching about giant jewel gates.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such huge jewels don't exist even in small size today, so the teaching seems impossible.

steps.title: The student sees angels cutting the giant jewels
steps.stepSummary: Later, at sea, the student sees angels sawing huge jewels and learns they are for the gates of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some time later his ship sailed out to sea. He saw the מלאכי השרת sawing precious stones and pearls. He asked them: Who are these for? They said: הקדוש ברוך הוא will set them up in the gates of ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows that רבי יוחנן was right. The student sees the giant jewels with his own eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels confirm exactly what רבי יוחנן taught. Now the student has 'proof,' which sets up how he will react when he comes back.

phrases.english: Some time later, his ship sailed out to sea.
He saw the ministering angels
who were sawing precious stones and pearls.
He said to them: Who are these for?
They said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined
to set them up in the gates of Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the student's mockery: the jewels really exist.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching about the jewel gates.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The angels sawing the jewels and saying they are for ירושלים's gates.

steps.title: The student 'confirms' רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The student comes back and tells רבי יוחנן: teach, it suits you, because I saw exactly what you said.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he returned, he found רבי יוחנן sitting and teaching. He said to him: רבי, teach, it is fitting for you to teach. Just as you said, so I saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The student now 'supports' רבי יוחנן. This sets up the next move, where רבי יוחנן shows why this kind of support is really disrespect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, these are words of praise, like the old man's 'well said.' But the student's support depends on his own eyes: he trusts רבי יוחנן only because he checked. This is the case רבי זירא meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach, for it is fitting for you to teach
Just as you said, so I saw

phrases.english: When he returned, he found Rabbi Yochanan
sitting and teaching.
He said to him: My teacher,
teach, for it is fitting for you to teach.
Just as you said, so I saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The student reports back with 'support' based on what he saw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The student praises רבי יוחנן only after confirming his words by sight.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rebukes and punishes the student
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן calls him an empty one: had you not seen, you would not have believed, so you are mocking the חכמים. He looks at him and turns him into a pile of bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Empty one! If you had not seen, you would not have believed? You are one who mocks the words of the חכמים! He set his eyes on him and made him into a pile of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains that the student's 'support' is really mockery, and he punishes him severely. This ends the story and answers רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man agreed out of trust, so it was real support. The student agreed only because he saw it himself, which shows he never trusted the חכמים' words. That is the 'support' that counts as אפקירותא.

keyTerms.meaning: One who mocks the words of the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: Agreeing with a חכם out of trust is honor. 'Agreeing' only after checking with your own eyes shows you never believed him, and that is the disrespect of an אפיקורס.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the student was punished for saying the words 'just as you said, so I saw.' He was punished for the attitude behind them: he would not believe the חכמים without seeing for himself.

phrases.english: He said to him: Empty one!
If you had not seen, you would not have believed?
You are one who mocks the words of the Sages!
He set his eyes upon him
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן looked at him in anger.

phrases.english: and made him into a pile of bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: רֵיקָה! אִם לֹא רָאִיתָ לֹא הֶאֱמַנְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Exposes the student's praise as mockery and concludes the story.
steps.whyThisMatters: This draws the line רבי ירמיה asked about: the difference between real support and disguised disrespect is whether you trust the חכמים' words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Praise that comes only after seeing with your own eyes is really mocking the חכמים, and that is אפקירותא.

steps.title: A ברייתא says people will be giants, so how will they fit through the gates?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: in the future people will be 200 אמות tall (רבי מאיר) or 100 אמות tall (רבי יהודה). That seems to clash with רבי יוחנן's gates of only 20 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'And I made you go upright (קוממיות)'. רבי מאיר says people will be 200 אמות tall, twice the height of אדם הראשון. רבי יהודה says 100 אמות, like the היכל and its walls, as it says: 'Our sons are like tall plants… our daughters like carved corners, in the shape of a היכל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's teaching about the gates. If people will be so tall, gates 20 אמות high are far too small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the huge jewels would have openings only 20 אמות high. Both opinions in the ברייתא make people at least 100 אמות tall, so they could not walk through such gates. This is a real contradiction, not just a question.

keyTerms.meaning: Upright; read here as 'two heights' (two קומות)
The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: They raised an objection: "And I made you go upright":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:13

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: two hundred cubits,
like two heights of Adam, the first man.
phrases.notes: The word קוממיות sounds like it holds two קומות, two heights.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: one hundred cubits,
matching the Sanctuary and its walls,
as it is said: "For our sons are like plants
grown tall in their youth;
our daughters like carved corners,
in the form of a Sanctuary, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 144:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of the student and returns to challenge רבי יוחנן's teaching about the gates
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the gate openings will be 20 אמות high
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If people will be 100 or 200 אמות tall, a 20-אמה opening cannot serve as their gate

steps.title: The 20-אמה openings are only windows for air
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן was talking about windows that let in air, not the doorways people walk through.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן spoke of those openings, he meant the windows where the wind comes in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The small openings are air windows, so the giant people do not need to fit through them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction depended on reading the 20-אמה openings as gates for people. By explaining them as wind openings, the גמרא leaves room for much taller doorways. Both the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן now stand.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yochanan said it,
he meant the windows where the wind enters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The openings were the gates people enter through
steps.terutzMaskana: They are wind windows; the gates for people are taller
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's 20-אמה openings are air windows, so they do not clash with the giant height of people in the future.

steps.title: What does 'its leaf for healing' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic. What is meant by the words 'ועלהו לתרופה' in the vision of the river coming out of the בית המקדש?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'and its leaf for healing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a פסוק in יחזקאל. It is setting up a dispute about how to read the word לתרופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the leaves of the trees by the river will be 'לתרופה'. The גמרא wants to know what kind of healing this is, and whether the word hides a deeper reading.

phrases.english: What is "and its leaf for healing"?
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 47:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the פסוק about the river (step 9) and asks about its last words, the healing leaves
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of healing the word לתרופה refers to

steps.title: Healing the upper mouth or the lower mouth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבודימי and רב חסדא read לתרופה as 'להתיר פה', to open a mouth. One says it means the upper mouth (healing mutes), and the other says the lower mouth (healing barren women).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבודימי and רב חסדא argue. One says: to open the upper mouth. The other says: to open the lower mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. Both break the word לתרופה into 'להתיר פה', but they disagree about which 'mouth' is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions read the word as a short form of 'להתיר פה'. The 'upper mouth' is the mouth used for speech, so the leaves heal mutes. The 'lower mouth' is a polite way to describe the womb, so the leaves heal barren women.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי וְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avudimi and Rav Chisda disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר, לְהַתִּיר פֶּה שֶׁל מַעְלָה;
phrases.english: one said: to open the upper mouth;
phrases.notes: He splits לתרופה into להתיר פה. The upper mouth means helping a mute person speak.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר, לְהַתִּיר פֶּה שֶׁל מַטָּה.
phrases.english: and one said: to open the lower mouth.
phrases.notes: A polite way to talk about the womb, so the leaves heal barren women.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר, לְהַתִּיר פֶּה שֶׁל מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לתרופה means 'להתיר פה': either healing mutes or healing barren women
steps.confusionAlert: The 'lower mouth' does not mean a second mouth on the body. It is a gentle way of referring to the womb.

steps.title: Another dispute: mutes, barren women, or real medicine
steps.stepSummary: A parallel dispute is reported. חזקיה says the leaves heal mutes, בר קפרא says they heal barren women, and רבי יוחנן says they are actual medicine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: חזקיה says it is to open the mouth of mutes. בר קפרא says it is to open the mouth of barren women. רבי יוחנן says it is real healing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, matching dispute. It adds a third view: רבי יוחנן reads the word simply, as real medicine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה and בר קפרא repeat the two readings from the previous step, now with clear names attached. רבי יוחנן is new: he does not break up the word, and he takes 'healing' at face value.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated, introducing a parallel teaching

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Chizkiyya said: to open the mouth of mutes;

phrases.aramaic: בַּר קַפָּרָא אָמַר לְהַתִּיר פֶּה עֲקָרוֹת,
phrases.english: bar Kappara said: to open the mouth of barren women;
Rabbi Yochanan said: for actual healing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a parallel dispute that matches step 20 and adds a third view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three views: the leaves heal mutes, they heal barren women, or they are literal medicine (רבי יוחנן)

steps.title: What extra meaning does the word לתרופה carry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again what לתרופה means, now that רבי יוחנן reads it as real medicine.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'for healing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. It is setting up a further explanation of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the leaves are real medicine. The גמרא now asks what לתרופה means according to his view: what exactly will this medicine do?

phrases.english: What is "for healing"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about רבי יוחנן's reading in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יוחנן's 'real medicine' view, what the word לתרופה refers to

steps.title: Beauty for the faces of those who learn with their mouths
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads לתרופה as 'לתואר פנים', for the beauty of the face of 'בעלי הפה', the people of the mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: it is for the beauty of the face of the masters of the mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the follow-up question. He finds a new short form hidden in the word לתרופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He explains רבי יוחנן's view: the 'medicine' is for 'תואר פנים של בעלי הפה', beauty for the faces of the חכמים who used their mouths to learn תורה. The word לתרופה is read as a short form of this phrase. So this is not a separate opinion; it spells out what רבי יוחנן's real medicine does.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of the mouth, people who use their mouths for תורה

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
for the beauty of the face of the masters of the mouth.
phrases.notes: Again a word play: לתרופה becomes לתואר פה. The 'masters of the mouth' are those who learn תורה out loud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לתרופה hints at 'לתואר פנים של בעלי הפה', beauty for the faces of those who learn תורה
steps.whatToRemember: The word לתרופה is read in three ways: healing mutes, healing barren women, or real medicine (רבי יוחנן). רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains that this real medicine gives beauty to the faces of those who learn תורה.

steps.title: Darkening the face for תורה brings shining in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה ברבי סימון teaches that someone who wears himself out over תורה in this world until his face looks dark will have his face made to shine by הקדוש ברוך הוא in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה ברבי סימון taught: Anyone who blackens his face over תורה in this world, הקדוש ברוך הוא will make his brightness shine in עולם הבא, as it says: 'His appearance is like the לבנון, choice as the cedars.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the face, continuing the idea of a beautiful face from the last step. It promises shining brightness in עולם הבא to someone who toils in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 spoke of 'תואר פנים', beauty of the face. Here that idea is tied to a reward: the face that got dark and tired from learning becomes bright later. The פסוק describing a radiant appearance is the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Blackens his face; wears himself out until his face looks dark
עולם הבא, the World to Come

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Simon taught:
Anyone who blackens his face
phrases.notes: He means someone who works so hard at learning that his face looks dark and worn out.

phrases.english: over words of Torah in this world,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַבְהִיק זִיוָיו לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes his brightness shine in the World to Come,
as it says: 'His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 5:15

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the beautiful face from step 23 with a new teaching about reward for Torah toil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who darkens his face over תורה in this world will shine in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Starving oneself for תורה brings being satisfied in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום ברבי חנילאי teaches that someone who goes hungry for the sake of learning תורה in this world will be fully satisfied by הקדוש ברוך הוא in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום ברבי חנילאי said: Anyone who starves himself over תורה in this world, הקדוש ברוך הוא will satisfy him in עולם הבא, as it says: 'They will be filled from the richness of Your house, and You will give them to drink from the river of Your delights.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second teaching with the same pattern: what you give up for תורה now, you get back in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 was about the face; this step is about hunger. Going without food for learning is paid back with being filled and given drink, as the פסוק describes.

keyTerms.meaning: Starves himself, goes hungry on purpose

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chanilai said:
Anyone who starves himself
over words of Torah in this world,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׂבִּיעוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, satisfies him in the World to Come,
as it says: 'They will be filled from the richness of Your house,
and You will give them to drink from the river of Your delights.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 36:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching to step 24, same pattern of sacrifice for תורה now and reward later.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who goes hungry for תורה in this world will be satisfied in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Every righteous person will receive a full handful
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי, arriving from ארץ ישראל, teaches that in the future הקדוש ברוך הוא will give every צדיק a full 'load' or handful, based on the פסוק 'day by day He loads for us'.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: In the future God will give every single righteous person His full handful, as it says: 'Blessed is ה׳, day by day He loads for us; God is our salvation, Selah.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a new teaching about how big the reward of the צדיקים will be. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He learns from the word יעמס ('He loads') that the reward is described as a full load, a full handful. As אביי's question shows, this is understood as God's own handful, which leads to the problem of size.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
In the future, is going to
His full load, his full handful
He loads, He carries a burden

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
In the future the Holy One, Blessed be He, will give
to each and every righteous person His full handful,
phrases.notes: 'His' here means God's own handful. That is what אביי will question next.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בָּרוּךְ ה׳ יוֹם יוֹם יַעֲמָס לָנוּ
phrases.english: as it says: 'Blessed is ה׳, day by day He loads for us;
God is our salvation, Selah.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of reward for צדיקים, now describing its size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every צדיק will receive a full handful (load) from הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: אביי asks how anyone could receive God's handful
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב דימי: how can you say that? The פסוק says God measured the waters in His palm and the heavens with His span, so God's handful is far too huge for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is it possible to say that? Doesn't it already say: 'Who measured the waters in His palm, and set the heavens with His span?'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב דימי's teaching, using a פסוק that shows how enormous God's 'hand' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If God's palm holds all the waters and His span measures the heavens, then 'His full handful' would be as big as the world. אביי finds it impossible that a single person could receive something that size.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really possible to say so?
But hasn't it already been said?
The hollow of the hand, palm
A span (distance from thumb to pinky)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And is it possible to say so?
But hasn't it already been said:
'Who measured the waters in the hollow of His hand,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 40:12

phrases.english: and set out the heavens with His span?'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר כֵּן? וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב דימי's teaching in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that every צדיק gets God's full handful
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: God's hand measures the waters and heavens, so His handful is far too vast for a person to receive.

steps.title: רב דימי answers that each righteous person gets 310 worlds
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers אביי: you must not be familiar with אגדה. In ארץ ישראל they teach in the name of רבא בר מרי that every צדיק will receive 310 worlds, from the word יש, whose גימטריא is 310.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Why are you not familiar with אגדה? For they say in the West in the name of רבא בר מרי: In the future God will give every single righteous person 310 worlds, as it says: 'To give those who love Me יש as an inheritance, and I will fill their treasuries.' The word יש in גימטריא equals 310.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי defends his teaching. He says the huge size is not a problem at all, because another teaching shows each צדיק gets 310 whole worlds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי thought a reward the size of God's handful was impossible. רב דימי shows from a known teaching that the reward really is that enormous: 310 worlds. The number comes from יש, where י is 10 and ש is 300.

keyTerms.meaning: You are not familiar with, not at home in
אגדה, the non-legal teachings of חז"ל
The number value of the letters of a word

steps.whatToRemember: The reward of צדיקים is beyond our imagination: each one receives 310 worlds, learned from the גימטריא of יש.

phrases.english: He said: What is the reason
that you are not familiar with aggada?
For they say in the West
in the name of Rava bar Mari:
In the future the Holy One, Blessed be He, will give
to each and every righteous person
three hundred and ten worlds,
as it says: 'To give those who love Me yesh as an inheritance,
and I will fill their treasuries.'
phrases.notes: משלי 8:21

phrases.english: 'Yesh' in gematria is three hundred and ten.
phrases.notes: The letter י is worth 10 and ש is worth 300, so together they make 310.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 27 and defends רב דימי's teaching in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise and shows it is supported by another teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed a reward as big as God's handful could not be given to a person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reward really is that vast, as shown by the teaching that each צדיק gets 310 worlds.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: You are measured out in the same measure you give
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: God measures out to a person in the same measure that person measured out to others. He learns this from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר says, in the measure a person measures out, he is measured out to, as it says: 'In full measure, when You send her away, You contend with her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that is connected to רב דימי's teaching about God giving a 'load' to every צדיק. רבי מאיר says that a person's reward or punishment matches what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads the unusual word בְּסַאסְּאָה as 'a סאה for a סאה': whatever measure you use, the same measure is used for you. This is the same idea behind רב דימי's teaching, so it will run into the same problem אביי raised.

keyTerms.meaning: In the measure a person measures out to others
A standard measure of volume; here it is used as a picture of 'measure for measure'

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Meir says,
In the measure that a person measures out, they measure out for him,
as it is written: 'In full measure, when You send her away, You contend with her.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:8. The odd word בְּסַאסְּאָה is read as 'a סאה for a סאה', meaning you get back in the same measure you gave.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא: רבי מאיר אומר, במדה שאדם מודד מודדין לו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא about measure for measure, which ties in with רב דימי's idea of God giving a 'load' to the צדיק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God repays a person in the same measure that the person used toward others, based on the reading 'a סאה for a סאה'.

steps.title: רבי יהושע objects: God's handful is far too big
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע asks how this can be true. If a person gives a poor man his handful, would God give him God's handful in עולם הבא? God's 'span' measures the whole heavens, so that would be far too much.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: Is it possible to say this? A person gives his handful to a poor man in this world, and הקדוש ברוך הוא gives him His handful in עולם הבא? But it says, 'He measured the heavens with His span'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע challenges רבי מאיר's rule. If the measure really matches, then a small gift to a poor person would earn God's enormous 'handful', which makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is about size. A person's handful is tiny, but God's 'span' is big enough to measure the heavens. So 'measure for measure' with God's hand seems to give a ridiculously huge reward. This is the same question אביי asked רב דימי in Step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really possible to say this? An expression of strong surprise or objection
His full handful, or as much as he can carry
A span, the distance from the thumb to the little finger

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 27. There it was אביי challenging רב דימי. Here it is רבי יהושע challenging רבי מאיר, but the question is the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
And is it possible to say so?
A person gives his full handful
to a poor man in this world,
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives him
His full handful in the World to Come?
But isn't it written: 'He measured the heavens with the span'!
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 40:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's measure-for-measure rule from Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's rule that God measures out to a person in the same measure the person used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: God's 'span' measures the heavens. If God matches a person's handful with His own handful, the reward would be impossibly large, so the rule cannot be meant literally.

steps.title: רבי מאיר answers: Which is greater, God's good or His punishment?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers with a question. Don't you also have to accept this? Which of God's measures is greater, the measure of good or the measure of punishment? This sets up an argument that continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you, do you not say so? Which measure is greater: is the measure of good greater, or the measure of punishment?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר starts defending his rule by asking רבי יהושע a pointed question. This line is setting up an argument that the גמרא will finish in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is turning the question around. He is preparing to show that God's measure of good is greater than His measure of punishment. If God punishes even on a large scale, then He certainly rewards on a huge scale. The full proof has not come yet; here he only asks the opening question.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means 'not', so 'and you, do you not say so?'
God's measure of good, meaning reward

phrases.english: And you, do you not say so?
phrases.notes: Now רבי מאיר is answering רבי יהושע: 'Don't you also have to agree with this?'

phrases.english: Which measure is greater:
is the measure of good greater
or the measure of punishment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי מאיר begins his answer to רבי יהושע's objection in Step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rhetorical question that opens a קל וחומר argument (finished in the next part of the גמרא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע thought that a reward on the scale of God's handful is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר is about to argue that God's measure of good is greater than His measure of punishment, so a huge reward is really possible.
